findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The only certified food protection manager was not present during the visit. There wasn't any cooking occurring, however, the facility was in the process of butchering meats on site. Any time food handling, cooking, or preparation is occurring, a CFPM is needed. Ensure that there is at least two employees who are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The cove base is pulling away from the wall (right of kitchen’s handsink). Ensure that the coving is resealed to prevent the accumulation of unwanted debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The follow areas are in need of recaulking:
- the handsink in the men’s bathroom 
- the triple sink inside of the meat room

In addition, the cove base is pulling away from the wall (right of kitchen’s handsink). Ensure that sinks are recaulked and that the cove base is resealed to prevent accumulated debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Baked potatoes stored in the heat and serve cooler (floor cooler) were observed without date marking. There should be either a sell by date or preparation date indicated on the packaging of the food. The items should be held for no longer than 7 days of preparation. A label was created with the correct use-by-date. Ensure that cooked and cooled items served for grab-and-go service are date marked and never held for longer than 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: A gallon of unopened whole milk stored in the walk in cooler was observed to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date (2/24/2025). Discussed and shown to the PIC and the gallon of milk was discarded. Ensure that milks stored in house never exceed the manufacturer's use-by-date.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.15: inspector observed the employee go from food prep to the walk in cooler and back to food prep with no glove change. Gloves were changed and hands were washed. Ensure that gloves are changed and hands are washed any time there is an interruption in operation. 

(A) If used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD or with raw animal FOOD, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-602.11: Inspector observed grab and go items to not include complete labels. Provide labels according the code requirements.

(A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. Pf (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observe employee to make sani bucket utilizing the hand sink. Hand sink’s are for handwashing ONLY. Cease practice. Discussed with employee. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed fans on ceiling of the meat prep area in back to have dust accumulation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 5/13/21 and 9/13/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed pizza chest freezer (“Blue Bunny” freezer) to have a large accumulation of frost. Ensure routine de-frosting of freezer in order to hinder frost build-up.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following NonFOOD-contact areas to have dust and debris:
1. Fans on ceiling of the meat prep area in back have dust accumulation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 5/13/21.
2. Dust on fans inside reach-in cooler near the big double doors/by water fountains. 
3. Fan on floor of the customer meat display counter area has accumulation of dust.

Ensure routine cleaning of NonFOOD-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed fans in walk-in cooler and fans in meat prep area in back to have large accumulation of dust. Ensure routine cleaning to avoid dust accumulation on fans.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed both the back deli meat prep area hand sink and 3 compartment sink in this area to have caulk missing between sinks and wall. Discussed caulking with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/29/20.

Observed both men and women's bathrooms to have caulk coming away from hand sink and wall. Discussed re-caulking with PIC.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler's licenses in public health folder. Discussed keeping copies of food handler's licenses with the certified food manager licenses in the folder. Ensure copies are kept at facility.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(2) (Pf) PIC does not demonstrate the responsibility of preventing the transmission of foodborne disease by employees that may cause food borne disease. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(C)(2).

Observed facility to lack signed employee health reporting agreements. Discussed importance of document and that all employee who handle food within the facility must sign document. Inspector will follow-up on 2/7/20.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11  (Pf) Establishment does not have procedures for employees to follow when responding to discharging of vomitus or fecal matter. Provide procedures to comply with this section of the code. Reference 2-501.11.

Observed facility to lack a policy or procedure for illness clean-up regarding Norovirus. Provided paperwork with PIC. Discussed policy procedure and suggested keeping paperwork in an area where employee may readily find. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-202.12  (Pf) Hot water not available in women's bathoom hand sink. Provide water of at least 100 deg F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. Reference 5-202.12.

Observed women's bathroom (duel customer and employee bathroom) to lack hot water. Discussed repairs with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 2/7/20.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11  (Pf) Packaged foods not properly labeled. Provide proper labeling.  Reference 3-201.11.

Observed facility to have a local rub, "Marty's Rub It Raw!", on shelves that is contained in deli-style containers not hermetically sealed. Additionally, rub does not have labeling information as to where item was processed or packaged. General comments provides contact information of product. No permitting information is available at the time of inspection. All foods must be processed and packaged in an approved, permitted, and inspected facility and it is unknown whether this product is at this time. Rubs were pulled from shelves voluntarily and will not be offered for sale until information is received. Inspector will follow-up on 2/7/20.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11  (Pf) Working container of mineral oil not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

Observed a working container of mineral oil to be unlabeled in the back meat prep area of deli. PIC stated it was formerly labeled but it is difficult to keep the label attached due to the nature of the oil content. Discussed various ideas to keep label attached. COS.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-602.11  (C) Prepackaged baked goods are not properly labeled. Label with: 1) common name of food, 2) ingredients, 3) net quantities, 4) name and address of packager, 5) food allergens, 6) nutrition labeling, 7) salmonid fish additives used. Reference 3-602.11.

Observed in-house baked goods to lack appropriate ingredient or allergen labeling on products (located near cash registers). Some products contained proper labeling; however, many did not. Discussed ingredient and allergen labeling with PIC.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed in-use wiping cloths to be stored outside of sanitization buckets. Discussed with PIC that all in-use wiping rags must be held within sanitization buckets of appropriate concentration and regularly changed, as needed. PIC was in compliance. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Caulk of the back deli meat prep area hand sink and 3 compartment sink were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed both the back deli meat prep area hand sink and 3 compartment sink to have caulk coming away from the walls. Discussed re-caulking with PIC.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program. Currently this has not taken place. Handout was given to the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete an accredited course prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment: Facility has a rub on the shelves labeled "Marty's Rub It Raw" and that is in deli style containers that are not hermetically sealed with no labeling information on where these items are processed or packaged. PIC states that it comes from Marty's Hawg Sauce--see General Comments section for contact information from label. No permitting information is available at the time of the inspection. All foods must be processed and packaged in an approved, permitted and inspected facility and it is unknown whether this product is at this time. Rubs were pulled from the shelf and will not be offerred for sale until information is received.
findings.citation_text: 3-201.11  (Pf) Packaged foods not properly labeled. Provide proper labeling.  Reference 3-201.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1) Carrot cakes with cream cheese frosting that is made on site is observed held at ambient air temperature next to the register. Carrot cakes were voluntarily pulled from the shelves and will not be sold. It was discussed that cream cheese frosting must be held at 41F or below at all times unless food safety testing information has been obtained on this product.

2) Ground beef in the meat department case was probed at an internal temperature of 45F. Beef was ground yesterday. Thermometer when placed between two steaks in the middle of this cooler read 42F. Thermometer at the ground beef end read 40F and the thermometer at the opposite end read 50F. PIC stated that this cooler may be in defrost. Ensure that thermometers are accurate and cooler is holding foods at internal temperatures of 41F or below at all times. Cooler will be adjusted as needed.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was voluntarily pulled from shelves and will not be sold. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed several open, in use meats in the deli that are either not date marked or marked with dates that exceed the 7 days allowed for these products. Items include: PAP loaf with a use by date of 9/13, souse with a use by date of 9/17, honey turkey with a use by date of 9/17, pineapple ham with a use by date of 9/13, and several small portions with no date. There are also two hams with use by dates of 10/4 and 10/10 which exceed the 7 days allowed for TCS foods. Items were discarded or re-dated as needed to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment: Baked goods next to the register do not have ingredient or allergen labeling on the products. Provide this information in addition to the information already provided on the current labels.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11  (C) Prepackaged baked goods are not properly labeled. Label with: 1) common name of food, 2) ingredients, 3) net quantities, 4) name and address of packager, 5) food allergens, 6) nutrition labeling, 7) salmonid fish additives used. Reference 3-602.11.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Spray bottle of mineral oil found without a label located on shelf across from display case. Labeled at the time of inspection. 

->Working container of ***** not properly labeled. Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wet wiping cloths were noted stored at room temperature on counter across from display case in the deli. 

->Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed leak underneath the handwashing sink. Repair the leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed chemicals stored with seasonings. The chemical bottles were removed and must be stored separate.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: Observed an oil used in meat cutting rooms to have no label. Label bottles with common name.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: Observed a leak at the three compartment sink. Repair leak.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: Quat sanitizer is being used in the deli but there is no quat test strip available in the facility.  750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. Provide quat test strips. Quat test strips were ordered.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: A cup of single use spoons for sampling are stored with handles and eating ends mixed. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law. The spoons were faced.
